newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- The U.S. Federal Reserve has voted to keep interest rates where they are.
- Mexico's Telefonos de Mexico SA is preparing for competition in the country's telephone long-distance market.
- Omnipoint Communications and Primeco Personal Communications plan to offer a new kind of cellular service in New York at cheaper rates than conventional networks.
- Westinghouse Electric Corp will spin off industrial businesses to shareholders as an independent company.
- Retail stocks fell for a second day and goverment bond prices remained little changed.
- Cash flows to equity mutual funds fell 25 percent to $13 billion in October.
- Proponents of affirmative action programs use a racial discrimination suit against Texaco Inc as reason to keep the programs.
- The NASDAQ stock market has proposed tougher listing standards for companies.
- IBM Corp will buy Edmark Corp for $110 million.
- China has managed to achieve high growth and low inflation.
- British Prime Minister John Major rejected a court ruling that sets a maximum work week of 48 hours.
